2609.15007.title: ABSOL: Aggregated Bayesian Subsampling Orchestrated with LLMs
2609.15007.paper_summary: Large language models are increasingly used as natural-language interfaces to structured data, yet they remain unreliable when answers require consistent evidence conditioning, dependency-aware reasoning, and uncertainty estimation. Bayesian networks provide an explicit probabilistic reasoning layer, but learning useful structures from data remains costly and fragile at scale. We introduce ABSOL, a hybrid LLM-guided Bayesian network structure-learning framework that uses LLMs as bounded semantic guides. Across five discrete BN benchmarks spanning 27 to 1041 nodes, ABSOL is the only evaluated method to produce a viable graph on every benchmark, and achieves the highest Edge F_1 on every benchmark larger than 27 nodes with GPT-5.4. The four LLM augmentations, which contribute complementary semantic evidence to the statistical backbone, improve Edge F_1 over the non-LLM aggregation backbone by +0.23 on average. Complementary post-hoc refinement experiments suggest that these gains depend in part on limiting the LLM's authority over the final structure. Together, these results show that language-derived semantic knowledge can substantially improve scalable probabilistic structure learning when used as bounded guidance within a statistically grounded reasoning pipeline. The code for ABSOL is available at github.com/megagonlabs/absol-bn.
2609.15007.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型越來越多地被用作結構化數據的自然語言介面，但當答案需要一致的證據條件、依賴感知推理和不確定性估計時，它們仍然不可靠。貝葉斯網絡提供了一個明確的概率推理層，但從數據中學習有用的結構在規模上仍然成本高昂且脆弱。我們介紹了ABSOL，一個混合的LLM引導的貝葉斯網絡結構學習框架，該框架使用LLM作為有限的語義指導。在五個涵蓋27到1041個節點的離散BN基準測試中，ABSOL是唯一一個在每個基準上產生可行圖的方法，並且在每個節點數大於27的基準上以GPT-5.4達到了最高的邊緣F_1。四個LLM增強，為統計骨幹提供互補的語義證據，平均提高了邊緣F_1比非LLM聚合骨幹高出+0.23。互補的事後細化實驗表明，這些增益部分依賴於限制LLM對最終結構的權威性。綜合這些結果顯示，當作為統計基礎推理管道中的有限指導使用時，語言衍生的語義知識可以顯著改善可擴展的概率結構學習。ABSOL的代碼可在github.com/megagonlabs/absol-bn上獲得。
